newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda says still committed to N. American market.
newsitem.headline: Mazda says still committed to N. American market.

text.p: Japan's Mazda Motor Corp said on Friday that the planned consolidation of its North American operations was aimed at strengthening its business in the region through greater efficiency, and did not mean a lesser commitment to the market.

Japan's fifth-largest carmaker, which is one-third owned by Ford Motor Co, announced earlier that it planned to consolidate its North American operations, a move likely to lead to a 25 percent cut in its work force in North America.
"The planned consolidation is aimed at improving our business efficiency and thus strengthening our operations there," a spokesman in Tokyo told Reuters.

"Although the size (of the company's operations) will become smaller, we are not considering shrinking our business there... We've never thought about pulling out from the North American market," he said.
